messages.subject: Consensus peaks from 'processed' data in sparse mat
parts:
Hi Kylie,

I'm wondering if I'm missing something in processed data in Cardinal. I have sets of peak lists (essentially processed imaging data) where I've built a ProcessedMSImagingExperiment with a ppm of 3 as the data has decent mass resolution. In this case, the summary looks like this:

An object of class 'MSProcessedImagingExperiment'
  <267858 feature, 10000 pixel> imaging dataset
    imageData(1): intensity
    featureData(0):
    pixelData(0):
    run(1): test
    raster dimensions: 397 x 26
    coord(2): x = 2600..2996, y = 874..899
    mass range:  294.000 to 2505.982 
    centroided: TRUE 

There are 267,858 mass bins, almost all of these are noise, have intensity values very close to zero if we summarize by mean, or are empty. Is there an efficient way to reduce the dimension by intensity threshold, frequency filtering, or some other operation to arrive at a representative consensus m/z list that is much smaller and amenable to a not-processed version of the data? Probably the true number of peaks in this dataset is around 3000-5000. Thanks for any advice you may have.

Heath
